CONFLICTS.title: How many GCCs in Bengaluru?

a.txt: GCC companies with a centre in Bengaluru. Vestian, Jul 2025.

b.txt: GCC centres in Bengaluru. Zinnov, Jan 2026.

CONFLICTS.read: Both can be right: one counts companies, the other counts centres. The same Zinnov post counts 1,760+ centres in India by end-2025, while the FY26 landscape counts 3,728 units, another definitional gap.

CONFLICTS.title: Maharashtra's GCC target

a.txt: new centres, 4 lakh jobs. Cabinet approval, Sep 2025.

b.txt: centres, 4 lakh jobs by 2030. CBRE, Aug 2026.

CONFLICTS.read: Same job target, half the centres. We show both until the notified policy text is linked.

CONFLICTS.title: Karnataka's mid-market GCCs

b.txt: mid-sized GCC units in Bengaluru alone.

CONFLICTS.read: Both numbers are in the same press release. A city cannot hold more than its state, unless one counts companies and the other counts units.

KA.name: Karnataka GCC Policy 2024–29
KA.target: 500 new GCCs and ~3.5 lakh jobs by 2029
facts: 50% reimbursement of internship stipends, up to 1 lakh students
Beyond Bengaluru: 5-year electricity duty exemption, rent and EPF support
Property tax reimbursement; nano GCCs (5–50 staff) eligible
Approvals within 45 days

MH.name: Maharashtra GCC Policy 2025
MH.target: Sources disagree: 400 centres (Sep 2025) vs ~200 centres (CBRE, Aug 2026); both say 4 lakh jobs
facts: Capital subsidy linked to fixed capital investment
Payroll reimbursement for high-skilled staff
Rent and power tariff assistance; R&D and patent support
Interest subsidy in tier-2 regions

HR.name: Haryana GCC Policy 2026
facts: Capex reimbursement 50% (non-TOD Gurugram), 65% (TOD Gurugram) or 75% (other districts), paid over 10 years
Opex 50–65% for 5–9 years, capped at ₹75 L per 100 employees or ₹15 Cr a year
Up to ₹1 L per employee; R&D grants up to ₹50 Cr per centre
8% interest on delayed incentives. JLL's capex caps (₹2.5 Cr per 100 staff or ₹75 Cr leased) read inconsistently, so check the notified text

UP.name: Uttar Pradesh GCC Policy
facts: Level-1 in Noida or Ghaziabad: ₹20 Cr investment or 200 staff
Land subsidy 30–50%; 100% stamp duty exemption
5% interest subsidy; opex support for lease, bandwidth, cloud and power
Payroll and recruitment subsidies for specified groups

GJ.name: Gujarat GCC Policy 2025–30
GJ.date: Launched Feb 2025; Operational Guidelines 1.0 issued 3 Oct 2026
facts: Capex 20% (non-IT) or 30% (IT), up to ₹50 Cr; ₹200 Cr for mega projects
Opex 15%, up to ₹20 Cr; ₹400 Cr for mega projects
One-time 50% of CTC per new hire, up to ₹60k (women) or ₹50k (men); EPF support 5 years
7% interest subsidy; 100% electricity duty exemption for 5 years

RJ.name: Rajasthan GCC Policy 2025
facts: 30% salary reimbursement for 3 years, up to ₹1.25 L per employee and ₹10 Cr per GCC a year
Rent 50% for 3 years then 25% for 2, up to ₹5 Cr a year
Salary and rent support limited to the first 10 GCCs per size band
Capital subsidy 30% up to ₹10 Cr (investment route)

MP.name: Madhya Pradesh GCC Policy 2025
facts: Capex, payroll, upskilling and R&D incentives (rates not in summary)

AP.name: AP IT & GCC Policy 4.0 (2024–29)
facts: Recruitment, rental, power and employee incentives for GCCs
Rates set in separate operating guidelines

TG.name: Telangana GCC framework; new policy in drafting
facts: New policy expected to target AI, space, semiconductors, quantum and life sciences

MODELS.label: Employer of record
MODELS.note: Fastest start, no entity needed. A provider employs your staff for a monthly fee per person, so it gets expensive at scale. Usually a bridge for the first 20 to 50 people. (Our judgement)

MODELS.label: Build-operate-transfer
MODELS.note: A partner sets up and runs the centre, then transfers it to you. Check the partner's delivery receipts first. (Our judgement)

MODELS.label: Own entity
MODELS.note: You incorporate and hire directly. Most control and lowest long-run cost; slowest start. (Our judgement)
